In '''2009–10''', '''[[FC Barcelona]]''' started the new season with the prospect of winning six major competitions in the 2008–2009 season. They contested for the [[2009 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], [[2009 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]], [[2009 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]], [[2009–10 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], [[2009–10 La Liga|La Liga]], and the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. During the summer transfer window, the club swapped their top league goal scorer during the treble season, [[Samuel Eto'o]] to Italy's [[Inter Milan]] in exchange for [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]], along with [[Euro|€]]48 million, bringing the total to €69 million.
On 16 May, Barcelona claimed its 20th league title<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/05/16/n100516111030.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100519111246/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/05/16/n100516111030.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2010-05-19 |title=Barça 20th League Title |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2010-05-16 |access-date=2010-05-17}}</ref> with a then-record 99 points via a 4–0 victory over relegated side [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] to finish their 2009–10 season with four titles.

==Overview==
Over the summer of 2009, along with Ibrahimović, Barcelona reinforced their squad with the signings of [[Inter Milan]] defender [[Maxwell (footballer, born 1981)|Maxwell]], Brazilian club [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] forward [[Keirrison]] (sent on loan with [[Portugal|Portuguese]] club [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], then loaned out during the [[transfer window|winter transfer window]] to Italian side [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]]), and [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] team [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] defender [[Dmytro Chyhrynskyi]]. Continuing its tradition of using ''[[cantera]]nos'' on the first team, Barcelona manager [[Pep Guardiola]] also promoted four players from the youth reserves, [[Jonathan dos Santos]], [[Jeffrén Suárez|Jeffrén]], [[Andreu Fontàs]] and [[Marc Muniesa]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/09/n090901106503.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090904031113/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/09/n090901106503.html |archive-date=4 September 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Barcelona player [[Henrique (footballer, born October 1986)|Henrique]], previously on loan with [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], briefly rejoined the squad for the pre-season but was again loaned out, this time to [[Racing de Santander]].

==Off the field events==
On 23 September, it was discovered by [[Catalunya|Catalan]] newspaper ''[[El Periódico de Catalunya|El Periódico]]'' of an investigation into the daily lives of four possible candidates for the Barcelona presidential election in 2010. The investigation was authorized by FC Barcelona director general, Joan Oliver, who hired investigating company Metodo 3 to gather daily information on vice president of institution and assets administration Joan Franquesa, vice president for marketing and media Jaume Ferrer, vice president for finance and treasurer Joan Boix, and vice president for sport Rafael Yuste between late March and early April 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=es&sl=es&tl=en&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.sport.es%2Fdefault.asp%3Fidpublicacio_PK%3D44%26idioma%3DCAS%26idnoticia_PK%3D647815%26idseccio_PK%3D803 |title=Google Traducir |language=es |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref> Oliver stated in a press conference the next day at the [[Camp Nou]] that "Barça did no spying but were just protecting the entity of the club".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=es&sl=es&tl=en&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.sport.es%2Fdefault.asp%3Fidpublicacio_PK%3D44%26idioma%3DCAS%26idnoticia_PK%3D647562%26idseccio_PK%3D803 |title=Google Traducir |language=es |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

President [[Joan Laporta]] stated that "this happened five months ago. Certain events happened and when I found out about them, the corresponding explanations were given. These explanations were understood and accepted since no law was broken." He added that "it was understood that the reports that were asked for were within the limits of legality and were to protect the affected parties and the club. Therefore, the page was turned and the case was closed." Laporta also said that "we are better than we have ever been in our entire history in our methods of operation, and now, because they want to destabilise us, people drag up issues like these. We will continue the same way, because everyone does it as well. We are used to living under pressure and people trying to destabilise us... Barça is united and united we are unbeatable."

Barcelona manager Pep Guardiola stated that "he has shielded the squad from the scandal of the investigation" and that "the subject has not been spoken of in the locker room and even the captains have not mentioned it, there's total concentration."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=es&sl=es&tl=en&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.sport.es%2Fdefault.asp%3Fidpublicacio_PK%3D44%26idioma%3DCAS%26idnoticia_PK%3D654142%26idseccio_PK%3D803 |title=Google Traducir |language=es |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

On 11 November, vice-president Joan Franquesa handed in his resignation for "personal reasons". Continuing the turmoil in the Barcelona Board-Room.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=697407&sec=europe&cc=5901 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604122223/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=697407&sec=europe&cc=5901 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 June 2011 |title=Barcelona vice-president Joan Franquesa quits board – Europe – ESPN Soccernet |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2009-11-11 |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref> President Joan Laporta took action by restructuring the board of directors and making Albert Perrín, the new vice-president. Laporta stated "He was making changes for these individuals to get to know the best club better."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://translate.google.com/translate?prev=hp&hl=en&js=y&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.elmundodeportivo.es%2Fgen%2F20091113%2F53823700117%2Fnoticia%2Fsala-i-martin-se-convierte-en-nuevo-tesorero-y-albert-perrin-asciende-a-vicepresidente.html&sl=ca&tl=en&history_state0= |title=Google Translate |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

===Ballon d'Or & FIFA World Player of the Year===
On 1 December, ''[[France Football]]'' magazine announced [[Lionel Messi]] was the winner of the [[2009 Ballon d'Or]], thus making him the ninth player while playing at Barcelona and the first Argentine and ''canterano'' from [[La Masia]] to win the coveted footballer prize.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=fr&tl=en&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.francefootball.fr%2FFF%2Fbreves2009%2F20091201_015505_messi-un-sacre-historique.html |title=Google Translate |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/destacades/n091130108082.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091204142542/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/destacades/n091130108082.html |archive-date=4 December 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/12/n091130108085.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091204142557/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/12/n091130108085.html |archive-date=4 December 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Messi dedicated his triumph at the [[Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper]] to "my family, who have always been by my side and my teammates at Barça who've done everything to ensure I could win the award". He also addressed his teammates [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] and [[Andrés Iniesta]], who finished third and fourth respectively: "They've given everything for Barça and they deserve their recognition. If I'd had a vote I would have voted for any of the Barça players."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/12/n091201108100.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091205143752/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/12/n091201108100.html |archive-date=5 December 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 21 December, Messi was named [[2009 FIFA World Player of the Year]] at the [[:de:Kongresshaus Zürich|Kongresshaus Zürich]] in [[Zürich]]. Messi claimed the prize by a record vote with a considerable wide margin, receiving 1,073 votes to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] forward [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]'s 352 votes, who finished second after winning the [[2008 FIFA World Player of the Year|year]] before. Teammates Xavi and Iniesta finished in third and fifth respectively, closing out 2009 as one of the most memorable years in Barcelona history.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/destacades/n091221108480.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100413022345/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/destacades/n091221108480.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2010-04-13 |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2009-12-21 |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

On 16 January, Messi became the youngest player to score 100 official goals for the Catalan club. He achieved the feat by scoring a [[brace (sports)|brace]] in a league match vs [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at the Camp Nou. He stated, "It was a relief to get the goal" and "the truth is that with all the big things that have happened to me, well I'm not giving them too much importance. I just try and live quietly and normally and keep my eye on achieving more."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/01/n100117108833.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100120064751/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/01/n100117108833.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2010-01-20 |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2010-01-17 |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

On 16 May, Messi completed the 2009–10 as the [[2009–10 La Liga#Pichichi Trophy|Pichichi Trophy]] and the [[European Golden Shoe#1996 to present|European Golden Shoe]] winner with 34 league goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/05/16/n100516111045.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100519123147/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/05/16/n100516111045.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2010-05-19 |title=Messi La Liga Pichichi |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2010-05-16 |access-date=2010-05-17}}</ref> [[Víctor Valdés]] won the [[2009–10 La Liga#Zamora Trophy|Zamora Trophy]] for the best La Liga [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] of the season.

===[[International Federation of Football History & Statistics|IFFHS]] Awards===
On 13 January, the International Federation of Football History & Statistic named Xavi the 2009 World's Best Playmaker and both teammates Lionel Messi and Andrés Iniesta received second and fourth place respectively. Lastly, manager Pep Guardiola was named 2009 World Club Coach.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/01/n100113108761.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2010-01-13 |access-date=2010-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100116030921/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/01/n100113108761.html |archive-date=16 January 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==FIFA Club World Cup & season friendly==
On 6 November, director general Joan Oliver confirmed that Barcelona would play a friendly in Kuwait on 21 December against [[Kuwaiti Premier League|Kuwaiti]] club [[Kazma Sporting Club]] at [[Al-Sadaqua Walsalam Stadium]]. It took place after the [[2009 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] which was being hosted in the [[Middle East|same region]] by the [[United Arab Emirates]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/11/n091106107662.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801050907/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/11/n091106107662.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-08-01 |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06 }}</ref> The match finished 1–1 with both goals coming in the last 10 minutes of the match in front of a sold-out crowd that gathered 45 minutes ahead of the kick-off time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_09-10/arxiu_partits/amistosos/kazma_fcb/partit.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref> Barcelona received €1.7 million to participate in the match.<ref>{{cite web|author=Spain |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2009/11/06/1608949/barcelona-to-play-lucrative-friendly-against-kazma-sporting-club- |title=Barcelona To Play Lucrative Friendly Against Kazma Sporting Club in December |publisher=Goal |date=2009-11-06 |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

On 16 December, [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]] became the first player in history to score in six different club competitions during a single season. He scored in La Liga, Copa del Rey, UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup, Supercopa de España and the FIFA Club World Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/12/n091216108378.html |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=2009-12-16 |access-date=2010-03-06 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120801094744/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada09-10/12/n091216108378.html |archive-date=1 August 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 19 December, Barcelona was crowned FIFA Club World Cup champion with a 1–2 win over [[Argentina|Argentine]] club [[Estudiantes de La Plata|Estudiantes]] in the [[2009 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]], making it the sixth title they've won in 2009 and the first club to accomplish that feat within one calendar year known as [[The Sextuple]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_09-10/arxiu_partits/mundial_clubs/final/jornada01/Barcelona_estudiantes_lp/partit.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20100203031934/http://www.fcbarcelona.cat/web/english/futbol/temporada_09-10/arxiu_partits/mundial_clubs/final/jornada01/Barcelona_estudiantes_lp/partit.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2010-02-03 |title=FCBarcelona.cat |publisher=FC Barcelona |access-date=2010-03-06}}</ref>

==Competitions==

===Overall===
As in nine out of the last ten seasons, Barcelona is going to be present in all major competitions: [[2009–10 La Liga|La Liga]], the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] and the [[2009–10 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]]. The previous season's treble success means that Barcelona will also contest the [[FIFA Club World Cup]], the [[UEFA Super Cup]] and the [[Supercopa de España]]. The side will also be present in the [[Copa Catalunya]].<br />
